content: Fosaprepitant is indicated for use in adults and children aged 6 months and older to prevent both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC), including high-dose cisplatin, as well as moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (MEC). Chronic continuous administration of fosaprepitant is not recommended due to the lack of studies and the potential for changes in the drug interaction profile during prolonged use. Drug Interactions and Contraindications: 1. Chloramphenicol: Increases fosaprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraindicated. 2. Danazol: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 3. Darunavir: Increases fosaprepitant levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 4. Flibanserin: Fosaprepitant increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to risks of severe hypotension or syncope. 5. Lomitapide: Fosaprepitant significantly increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 6. Lonafarnib: Fosaprepitant increases lonafarnib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 7. Pimozide: Fosaprepitant increases pimozide levels by reducing its metabolism, raising the risk of QT interval prolongation. Contraindicated. 8. Ribociclib: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 9. Tipranavir: Increases fosaprepitant levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 10. Apalutamide: Decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce therapeutic efficacy. 11. Avapritinib: Fosaprepitant increases avapritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the avapritinib starting dose. 12. Axitinib: Fosaprepitant increases axitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor closely and adjust the dose as needed. 13. Bosutinib: Fosaprepitant increases bosutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Carbamazepine: Decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Ceritinib: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Cimetidine: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Clarithromycin: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Cobimetinib: Fosaprepitant increases cobimetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg daily. 20. Colchicine: Fosaprepitant increases colchicine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 21. Conivaptan: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Dihydroergotamine: Fosaprepitant increases dihydroergotamine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 23. Diltiazem: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Dronedarone: Fosaprepitant increases dronedarone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 25. Elacestrant: Fosaprepitant increases elacestrant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Eliglustat: Fosaprepitant increases eliglustat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustments may be required based on metabolic status. 27. Encorafenib: Fosaprepitant increases encorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half. 28. Entrectinib: Fosaprepitant increases entrectinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Enzalutamide: Decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Ergotamine: Fosaprepitant increases ergotamine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 31. Erythromycin (all forms): Fosaprepitant and erythromycin mutually increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Everolimus: Fosaprepitant increases everolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 33. Fedratinib: Fosaprepitant increases fedratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Fentanyl (all forms): Fosaprepitant increases fentanyl levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 35. Ibrutinib: Fosaprepitant increases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Interrupt ibrutinib therapy if strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are required short-term. 36. Idelalisib: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Infigratinib: Fosaprepitant increases infigratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Itraconazole: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Ivabradine: Fosaprepitant increases ivabradine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Ivosidenib: Decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Ketoconazole: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lemborexant: Fosaprepitant increases lemborexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Lovastatin: Fosaprepitant increases lovastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 44. Lurbinectedin: Fosaprepitant increases lurbinectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Midazolam (intranasal): Fosaprepitant increases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Mifepristone: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Naloxegol: Fosaprepitant increases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Nefazodone: Increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Neratinib: Fosaprepitant increases neratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Nirogacestat: Fosaprepitant increases nirogacestat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Olaparib: Fosaprepitant increases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose. 52. Omaveloxolone: Fosaprepitant increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose and monitor for adverse effects. 53. Pacritinib: Decreases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Pazopanib: Fosaprepitant increases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Clinical Recommendations: Avoid co-administration of fosaprepitant with drugs that are strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers unless absolutely necessary. Monitor patients closely for adverse effects or loss of therapeutic efficacy when co-administration cannot be avoided. Adjust dosages of affected drugs as per prescribing information to mitigate risks.
